bundle.guidance:
# End-User Guide

Help for people who did not choose this software and do not want to learn it.
They arrived stuck. The guide's only job is to unstick them in under a minute.

## Principles

1. **Answer the question in the heading.** Headings are the user's words —
   "I can't sign in", not "Authentication troubleshooting".
2. **One task, one card, one screenshot.** If a task needs two screenshots it
   is two tasks.
3. **Reassure.** Say what will happen before it happens, and say when
   something is safe to try.

## Layout grid

Single column at `max-width: 44rem` with `--space-xl` between tasks. Cards and
screenshot slots run full width. Type is large and lines are short on purpose;
never reduce `--size-body` to fit more on screen. Everything stacks cleanly on
a phone — no side-by-side layouts wider than two items.

## Typography

Nunito throughout, rounded and friendly, `--size-body` for prose and
`--line-body` for comfortable reading. Headings at `--size-h1` / `--size-h2` /
`--size-h3`, sentence case, never all caps. Use bold for the exact label of a
button or menu item the user must find; never use italics for emphasis.

## Colour usage

Warm off-white page, white cards, orange accent
(`--color-brand-primary`) for the step badges, the "Do this" card rule and
links. Contrast is deliberately high — the reader may be on a phone outdoors.
Status green confirms, amber cautions, red warns about something that cannot
be undone. Never rely on colour alone: every coloured element also carries a
word.

## Charts

Chart.js, rarely. Only for something the user personally owns — storage used,
messages sent, days remaining. Single series, bar or doughnut, with the value
printed as text next to it. Never show a chart the reader cannot act on.

## Diagrams

Mermaid `flowchart TD` for "which of these is your situation?" branching, at
most five nodes, with plain-language labels. Otherwise prefer numbered steps.

## Components and when to use each

- `do-this` — the primary action card: what to do, in one or two steps. Every
  task page has exactly one, near the top.
- `screenshot` — a captioned image slot. The caption says what to look at, not
  what the image is.
- `faq-item` — a question and its short answer, collapsed into a list at the
  bottom of a page.
- `tip` — a friendly aside. Optional information only; nothing required to
  finish the task may live here.

## Do / don't

- **Do** use "you" and the present tense.
- **Do** tell the reader what success looks like: "Your name appears in the
  top right."
- **Don't** use jargon without a plain-language gloss in the same sentence.
- **Don't** apologise for the software or explain why it behaves this way.
- **Don't** put a required step inside a tip or a footnote.

components.name: do-this
components.description: The primary action card for a task.
components.when_to_use: Exactly one near the top of every task page.
components.html:
Do this

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Choose Reset password and check your email.

You are signed in and your name appears in the top right.

components.name: screenshot
components.when_to_use: One per task. The caption says what to look at.

components.name: faq-item
components.description: One question with a short answer.
components.when_to_use: Grouped at the bottom of a page, for things that are not the main task.
components.html:
What if the email never arrives?

Check your spam folder, then try again in five minutes.

components.name: tip
components.when_to_use: Never for a required step. Optional shortcuts and reassurance only.
components.html: You can change this later — nothing here is permanent.

charts.notes: Only for something the reader owns; single series, value printed as text.
